root_idea.summary: Opening or displaying the front of the mouth as an expression of gladness, below the degree of full laughter.
root_idea.development: The facial action yields the Form V sense of a slight smile or laugh. Classical figurative usage extends the image of a faint opening or display to lightning showing through clouds and to a palm spadix splitting at its ends; a separate Form I expression is also attested for tasting.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form V verb is a distinct and directly supported public form.

senses.definition: To smile—to show the front of the mouth in a slight laugh, below full laughter.
senses.usage_conditions: Describes the beginning or lesser degree of ضحك and may involve opening the lips to display the teeth or laughing without sound. The Quranic occurrence is in the construction تَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكًا, smiling in response to what was said.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a figurative expression, to taste a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction مَا بَسَمْتُ فِي الشَّيْءِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of clouds, to display a faint flash of lightning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction describing a weak or intermittent showing of lightning through the clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm-tree spadix, to burst open at its extremities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage applied to the extremities of the palm spadix or spathe splitting apart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who smiles much; a frequent smiler.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet or intensive descriptive form derived from بَسَمَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The front teeth; possibly, by extension, the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Named as the place of smiling; the plural is مَبَاسِمُ, and the mouth sense is reported tentatively.

cautions: The Quranic form is attested once, at 27:19; the cloud, palm-spadix, tasting, and nominal uses are broader Classical Arabic evidence rather than additional Quranic senses.
